text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Relatives of the five Latvian pilots arrested in India sent a letter to President Guntis Ulmanis asking that he request an earlier start of legal proceedings by the Indian authorities.
- Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh signed an order subordinating the border guard to the interior ministry.

- According to preliminary estimates by the ministry of the economy, Latvia's GDP in 1996 increased by 2.5 percent. The ministry forecasts that next year, GDP may increase by 2.4 to 4.5 percent depending on economic and fiscal policy.
- The body responsible for selling appartments has started the privatisation of state-owned flats throughout the country.
- Electricity tariffs in Latvia are likely to grow by eight to nine percent from April 1.
- State-owned electricity firm, Latvenergo, said it needs some 500,000 to 600,000 lats fully to restore electricity to the regions hit by heavy snow falls.
- Estonian Tallinna Pank has bought the newly-issued shares of Saules Banka worth 780,000 lats or 20.1 percent of the bank's total amount shares.
